summary: Jens Braarvig is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He held a professorship at the University of Oslo (2003) and was attested as a professor at the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology in 2004.

Jens Peter Laut works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Succeeding Klaus Röhrborn in 2008, he held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 2008 to 2020.

Jens Schlieter specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Vienna and earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under Josef Simon, later serving as professor at the University of Bern (circa 2009).

Jens-Uwe Hartmann worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his Magister, PhD, and Habilitation across Munich and Göttingen, later serving as professor at Humboldt University, the Free University of Berlin, and the University of Munich (1999–2018).

Jeong-Eun Kim specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Kim earned a PhD from SOAS University of London in 2011, studying under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

Jerome Silbergeld is a scholar of sinology and history and archaeology. He earned his degrees from Stanford and the University of Oregon, later holding posts at the University of Washington (circa 1975–2001) and Princeton University (circa 2001–2018).

Jerzy Bańczerowski was a linguist who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań. He later served there as head of the Department of General and Comparative Linguistics (1969) and as professor from 1977 to 1991.

Jerzy Kuryłowicz was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Lviv and under Antoine Meillet, later holding academic posts at the University of Lviv (circa 1926–1946) and Jagiellonian University (circa 1946–1965).

Jessie Pons is a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Paris-Sorbonne University in 2011 and was attested as a Junior Professor at Ruhr University Bochum in 2019.
Jian Ouyang was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Yang Renshan. He founded and headed the China Institute of Inner Learning from circa 1922 to 1943.

Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He completed graduate studies at Nankai University and earned his doctorate at Harvard University under Tu Weiming and Robert M. Gimello, later serving as professor at the University of Arizona.
Jianming Hu works in Buddhist studies. Hu studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and was attested as a researcher at Komazawa University in 2015.

Jiayao An is a specialist in history, archaeology, and sinology who studied under Su Bai. She held posts at the Institute of Archaeology, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, and served as a special researcher and director of its Xi'an research office.
Jien Abe was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973) and served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.

Jigdal Dagchen Sakya was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teachers Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dilgo Khyentse. He held a post at the University of Washington from circa 1960 to 1963.

Jigme Chhoeda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Educated at Druk Sangag Choeling and Tango monasteries under several traditional teachers, he served as abbot of Tango Monastery and held Drapoi Lopen and Dorji Lopen posts in Bhutan.
Jigme Tenpai Nyima studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under Yongdong Shi, while also studying under traditional teacher Huixian (attested 2013).
Jikai Fujiyoshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He was affiliated with Kyoto University as a member (attested 1967) and served as a professor at Rissho University.

Jikidō Takasaki was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Savitribai Phule Pune University under V. V. Gokhale, he held professorships at the University of Tokyo and served as president of Tsurumi University (1992–2004).
